handbookNote: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision dated 7/24 i.e. July 2024), published by the Maine Department of the Secretary of State, Bureau of Motor Vehicles (BMV) -- fetched directly from the official maine.gov-hosted PDF at https://www.maine.gov/sos/sites/maine.gov.sos/files/inline-files/CDL%20Manual%20Rev.%207-24.pdf on 2026-08-22 (4.67MB PDF, full text extracted via pdftotext to scratchpad/me_cdl_research/me_cdl_manual_nolayout.txt, 5,996 lines); the digitalmaine.com-hosted mirror of the same manual (https://digitalmaine.com/context/bmv_docs/article/1000/viewcontent/MaineCommercialManual.pdf) sits behind an AWS WAF bot-challenge that blocks direct fetch tools, so the maine.gov copy was used instead as the authoritative official source. Also fetched and consulted: the official 'Maine Commercial Driver License Skills Test Addendum' at https://www.maine.gov/sos/sites/maine.gov.sos/files/inline-files/Addendum%20final.pdf on 2026-08-22 (covers Maine's phased transition to the AAMVA Modernized CDL Skills Testing standard: new Vehicle Inspection rules apply to skills-test applicants starting 11/1/2026, full modernized standard including Basic Control Skills takes effect 9/1/2027; confirms the CDL skills exam is split into three 30-minute segments -- Vehicle Inspection, Basic Control Skills, Road Test -- for 90 minutes total). Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Real exam mechanics: NEITHER the official Maine CDL manual NOR the official Skills Test Addendum discloses an exact knowledge-test question count or number-correct-to-pass for the general knowledge test or any endorsement test -- the manual states only that 'these tests consist of multiple choice questions pertaining to the information contained in the Commercial Driver License Manual' without giving a count. Several third-party test-prep sites (e.g. epermittest.com, dmv-written-test.com) converge on a claim of '50 questions, 40 correct (80%) to pass' for Maine's general knowledge test, but this could not be confirmed on any official maine.gov or digitalmaine.com source and is therefore NOT asserted as fact in this question bank -- per this project's no-default-values discipline this is explicitly hedged rather than presented as confirmed. What IS confirmed directly from the official Maine manual: the federally standardized 80% minimum passing score applies to all CDL knowledge tests (49 CFR 383.135(a), same as every other CDL-track state in this project); Maine's pre-trip vehicle inspection skills-test component requires the applicant to properly check at least 80% of the inspection items to qualify (this 80% figure is for the SKILLS test inspection checklist, not the knowledge test, and this bank keeps that distinction explicit rather than conflating the two); Maine has three CDL classes -- Class A (combination vehicles, GCWR 26,001+ lbs with a towed unit over 10,000 lbs GVWR, and holders may operate Class B and C vehicles with appropriate endorsements), Class B (single vehicle GVWR 26,001+ lbs or towing a unit not over 10,000 lbs, holders may also operate Class C), and Class C (any vehicle not meeting A/B definitions that is a CDL only if it carries an endorsement under 29-A MRSA Section 1253(3), e.g. passenger or hazmat); Maine recognizes six CDL endorsement knowledge tests -- N (tank vehicles only), H (hazardous materials), X (combined tank + hazmat), T (double/triple trailers -- the manual explicitly notes triple trailers are NOT allowed in Maine, so T in practice covers doubles only), P (passenger, for vehicles carrying over 15 passengers including the driver), and S (school bus, over 15 passengers including the driver); the N, H, X, and T endorsements are awarded on successful completion of the knowledge test alone, while P and S additionally require the full skills test; a school bus designed for 15 passengers or fewer uses a separate non-CDL 'Z' endorsement affixed to a regular (non-commercial) operator's license rather than a CDL, confirmed directly from the manual's own School Bus Endorsement Codes section; an accompanying driver for a CDL learner's permit holder must hold a license valid for the vehicle/endorsements being practiced, have held that license at least two years, occupy the seat beside the driver, and be at least 20 years old (22 if the vehicle is a bus or school bus); vision standards require 20/40 distance acuity in the better eye and a minimum 110-degree field of vision, with permits/licenses restricted to corrective lenses if that standard is met only with glasses/contacts; a $70.00 penalty fee applies for failing to cancel a scheduled skills-test appointment with at least 48 hours' notice; the hazardous materials TSA background-check/fingerprinting fee is $89.25, payable to the TSA agent, and hazmat endorsement eligibility requires U.S. citizenship or lawful-permanent-resident status plus a clean record against the TSA's permanently- and interim-disqualifying criminal offense lists; CDL disqualification penalties mirror the federal baseline -- at least 1 year CDL loss for a first BAC-.04%+/DUI/refusal/leaving-the-scene/CMV-felony offense (3 years if the vehicle was placarded for hazardous materials, life for a second such offense or for using a CMV to commit a controlled-substance felony), 60 days for two serious traffic violations in 3 years (120 days for three or more), 90 days for a first out-of-service-order violation (1 year for a second within 10 years, 3 years for a third), and 60/120 days/1 year respectively for first/second/third railroad-highway grade-crossing violations within 3 years; the off-street basic-control-skills course layout uses 10 cones, 10 flags, and 3 ropes with course lengths that scale by vehicle class and length (e.g. Class A vehicles 40 ft or less get a 72 ft course, over 40 but under 60 ft get 82 ft, 60 ft or more get 92 ft; Class B vehicles get vehicle length plus 10/15/20 additional feet depending on single/dual/tri rear axle configuration). Content-depth rationale: Maine uses the AAMVA-authored 2005 CDL Testing System base manual (same generation as Louisiana and Indiana, already built in this project) organized into the same 13 core sections -- Section 1 Introduction (paired with Maine-specific front matter: license classes, endorsements, disqualifications, TSA hazmat background-check detail -- layered into the licensing bucket), Section 2 Driving Safely (by far the largest section, split into two buckets for volume), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (the second-largest section, split into two buckets), Section 10 School Buses, Section 11 Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection, Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills, and Section 13 On-Road Driving. Some sections (Cargo, Tank Vehicles, Doubles/Triples) are naturally short in Maine's manual and their question buckets were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Maine manual or addendum text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers.
